subject: March 8 tokenization latency: technical readout, timeline, and committed fixes
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Han <claire.han@clearline.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: March 8 tokenization latency: technical readout, timeline, and committed fixes

Hi Claire / Clearline team,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the internal investigation into the March 8th tokenization latency you experienced. Attached is a concise RCA and our remediation plan (attachment: Clearline-March8-Incident-RCA.pdf). High-level summary below: 

- Impact: Elevated tokenization latency affecting ~0.6% of requests to the tokenization service between 03:02 and 03:38 UTC on 2028-03-08, causing transient increased tail latency for several Clearline routes.
- Root cause (short): A change in our batching heuristic + an edge-case in the sequence-length estimator caused suboptimal batch composition under a rare traffic mix; this exposed an untested kernel path that increased per-request GPU scheduling time.
- Customer-facing mitigations implemented within 3 hours: reverted the heuristic, applied a temporary request-level affinity flag for your account, and rolled a hotfix that bypasses the affected kernel path.

Committed next steps (detailed in attachment):
1) Permanent kernel fix and backward-compatible unit test (ETA: 2028-03-18)
2) Batching heuristic rewrite with zone-level safety limits and synthetic fuzz tests (ETA: 2028-03-25)
3) Account-level protections: static affinity option and an admin toggle for immediate fallbacks (ETA: 2028-03-15)
4) Post-deploy verification run with Clearline traffic replica and a joint validation call (scheduling link in related links)

Please review the attached PDF. We propose a follow-up technical readout on Monday 2028-03-13 at 10:00am PT to walk through the timeline, the fix, and the verification plan. If that slot doesn’t work, suggest a couple alternatives.

Apologies again for the disruption — keeping this from happening again is our highest priority.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Clearline-March8-Incident-RCA.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB), mitigation-runbook-v1.md (text)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Han <claire.han@clearline.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 8 tokenization latency: technical readout, timeline, and committed fixes

Diego — quick note: the RCA PDF is solid, one small ask: can we add the short-term mitigation timeline as a two-column table (time / action) on page 2 so customers can see exactly when each mitigation executed? Also include the monitoring queries (PromQL and log queries) we used for verification as an appendix.

I flagged the account-level admin toggle in the runbook as "high priority" — David, can your team confirm the rollback playbook is present and validated?

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Han <claire.han@clearline.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 8 tokenization latency: technical readout, timeline, and committed fixes

Hi Diego / Marissa,

Thank you for the fast turnaround and the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our ops and SRE teams after a quick read: 

1) Can you confirm whether any requests were dropped or only delayed? We saw retries in our logs but not obvious 5xx spikes.
2) For the account affinity toggle, is that scoped per-route or per-tenant? We want to understand any operator-induced blast radius.
3) Would it be possible to get a short (15‑minute) walkthrough of the mitigation-runbook and the verification queries before the Monday readout? Our SRE lead (ops@clearline.com) would join.

If those clarifications are straightforward we can sign-off on the RCA and move to joint verification. Monday at 10:00am PT works but ops would appreciate the short walkthrough beforehand (Friday preferred).

Best,
Claire Han
Head of Platform Reliability | Clearline Financial
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Han <claire.han@clearline.com>, Clearline Operations <ops@clearline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-12T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 8 tokenization latency: technical readout, timeline, and committed fixes

Claire — thank you, and great questions. Short answers up front:

1) No requests were intentionally dropped by Redwood. We observed elevated tail latency and client-side retries; there was no spike in 5xx responses tied to the event window after we correlate request ids. We include the verification artifacts and request-id samples in the appendix of the PDF.
2) The account affinity toggle is per-tenant with an optional per-route override. Default behavior is tenant-scoped to limit operator surface area; enabling per-route is available but gated behind an explicit confirmation step in the runbook.
3) Yes — we can run a 20-minute mitigation-runbook walkthrough on Friday 2028-03-12 at 2:00pm PT. I’ll share a calendar invite and the short runbook markdown (mitigation-runbook-v1.md) in the invite.

Action items we’re committing to now: 
- Friday 2028-03-12 14:00 PT: mitigation-runbook walkthrough (Redwood + Clearline ops) — invite sent.
- Monday 2028-03-13 10:00 PT: joint verification readout (timeline + post-deploy validation).
- ETA 2028-03-15: Account admin toggle deployed and available to Clearline via console, with rollback test documented.
- ETA 2028-03-18: Kernel patch deployed to canary and smoke-tested.

If anything urgent comes up before the walkthrough, ping me directly. We appreciate your partnership and will keep communications concise and evidence-driven.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
